title: Inertial fusion target fabrication cost and precision
bottleneck: Inertial fusion targets are precision-engineered capsules, layered deuterium-tritium ice inside high-density shells with nanometer surface tolerances, that must cost cents rather than thousands of dollars, since a plant consumes millions per year. Current targets are hand-assembled at national labs for hundreds of thousands of dollars each. Mass-manufacturing targets that survive injection into a reactor chamber at meters per second while remaining perfectly spherical is unsolved.
why_it_blocks: Target cost is a hard economic floor for inertial fusion. Even with high gain, million-dollar targets make electricity impossibly expensive, and no credible mass-production path has been demonstrated.
current_state: Lab target fabrication is exquisite but artisanal. Startups and labs are exploring injection molding and batch cryogenic layering, all at early stages.

sources.title: Reliable Nuclear Fusion Will Require New Heat- and Radiation-Resilient Materials
